    //==
    // # Derived functions for the IQuantity interface
    //
    // Bodies for the IQuantity interface declared in `quantities.concepts.plato`.
    // Ordering, interpolation, Double and Half all come from the `core-*` /
    // `algebra-*` libraries via
    // the inherited interfaces; only what is specific to the Amount projection is
    // added here. Pure expressions only; all values are immutable.

    //==
    // # IQuantity
    //
    // A one-dimensional measured amount (IValue, IComparable, IHashable, IAdditive,
    // IScalable, IInterpolatable) with an Amount projected to a raw Number.
    // Ordering (Lesser/Greater/Clamp/Between), MidPoint, LerpClamped, Double and
    // Half all come from CoreAlgebra via the inherited interfaces; only the
    // Amount-based sign/zero predicates and the same-type absolute value are
    // added here. IQuantity is deliberately not IArithmetic (multiplying two
    // quantities yields a different type), so no product helper is offered.

    // True when the underlying amount is exactly zero. (IQuantity is not INumerical,
    // so CoreAlgebra's IsZero does not apply.)
    IsZero(self: IQuantity): Boolean
        => self.Amount == 0.0;

    // True when the underlying amount is strictly greater than zero.
    IsPositive(self: IQuantity): Boolean
        => self.Amount > 0.0;

    // True when the underlying amount is strictly less than zero.
    IsNegative(self: IQuantity): Boolean
        => self.Amount < 0.0;

    // The sign of the quantity: 1 when positive, -1 when negative, 0 when zero.
    Sign(self: IQuantity): Integer
        => self.Amount.Sign;

    // The absolute value: the quantity with a non-negative amount.
    Abs(self: IQuantity): IQuantity
        => self.IsNegative ? self.Negative : self;

    // The magnitude of the gap between two quantities; always non-negative.
    AbsoluteDifference(a: IQuantity, b: IQuantity): IQuantity
        => (a - b).Abs;

    //==
    // # Geometric helpers for the IVector interface
    //
    // The geometry that sits on top of Dot and Magnitude: distances, projection and
    // rejection, reflection, angles between vectors, safe normalization, the 3D
    // cross-product neighbourhood, the 2D planar perp, and the validated Direction
    // factories. The component-wise machinery is in the sections above.

    //==
    // # IVector
    //
    // Fixed-arity numeric vectors
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_(mathematics_and_physics); INumerical,
    // IArithmetic, IIndexable<Number>, INormed, ILattice, IHashable) with a Dot product
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot_product). Magnitude and
    // MagnitudeSquared come from INormed; Min/Max are the component-wise lattice
    // operations. MidPoint and LerpClamped come from CoreAlgebra (IInterpolatable).
    // IVector is ILattice but not IClampable, so the box clamps below stay here.
    //
    // The former interface-gap is closed: IVector now declares FromComponents and
    // Broadcast alongside the inherited At/Count, so the component surface is
    // read-and-construct. Everything below the "component-wise lifting" banner —
    // the map/zip/fold combinators, the reductions (SumComponents, MinComponent,
    // AvgComponent), the arithmetic and lattice bodies, the INumericalLimits
    // elements, and the per-component lifts of the Number intrinsics — is derived
    // once here and applies to every implementing type.

    // The unit vector in the same direction. Precondition: non-zero magnitude.
    Normalize(self: IVector): IVector
        => self / self.Magnitude;

    // The straight-line distance between the tips of two vectors.
    Distance(a: IVector, b: IVector): Number
        => (a - b).Magnitude;

    // The squared distance between two vectors; avoids the square root when only
    // relative distances are compared.
    DistanceSquared(a: IVector, b: IVector): Number
        => (a - b).MagnitudeSquared;

    // True when b lies within the given radius of a (inclusive). Compares squared
    // distances, so no square root is taken.
    WithinDistance(a: IVector, b: IVector, radius: Number): Boolean
        => a.DistanceSquared(b) <= radius * radius;

    // The signed length of self projected onto onto. Precondition: onto is non-zero.
    ScalarProjection(self: IVector, onto: IVector): Number
        => self.Dot(onto) / onto.Magnitude;

    // The component of self parallel to onto
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_projection). Precondition: onto is
    // non-zero.
    ProjectOnto(self: IVector, onto: IVector): IVector
        => onto * (self.Dot(onto) / onto.Dot(onto));

    // The component of self perpendicular to onto. Precondition: onto is non-zero.
    RejectFrom(self: IVector, onto: IVector): IVector
        => self - self.ProjectOnto(onto);

    // Reflects self across the plane whose normal is given. Precondition: normal
    // is a unit vector.
    Reflect(self: IVector, normal: IVector): IVector
        => self - normal * (2.0 * self.Dot(normal));

    // The cosine of the angle between a and b: Dot divided by the product of
    // magnitudes. Preconditions: a and b are non-zero.
    CosineSimilarity(a: IVector, b: IVector): Number
        => a.Dot(b) / (a.Magnitude * b.Magnitude);

    // The unsigned angle between a and b, in [0, Pi]. The cosine similarity is
    // clamped to [-1, 1] before Acos so floating-point drift cannot produce a NaN.
    // Preconditions: a and b are non-zero.
    AngleBetween(a: IVector, b: IVector): Angle
        => a.CosineSimilarity(b).Clamp(-1.0, 1.0).Acos;

    // A vector in the same direction as self but with the given length.
    // Precondition: self is non-zero.
    ScaledToLength(self: IVector, length: Number): IVector
        => self.Normalize * length;

    // Restricts each component of self to the box spanned by lo and hi, using the
    // component-wise lattice operations. Precondition: lo <= hi component-wise.
    Clamp(self: IVector, lo: IVector, hi: IVector): IVector
        => self.Max(lo).Min(hi);

    // Restricts each component of self to [0, 1] using the vector's own Zero and
    // One elements (the component-wise analogue of CoreAlgebra's Saturate).
    Saturate(self: IVector): IVector
        => self.Max(self.Zero).Min(self.One);

    //==
    // # IVector — safe normalization and directions (normalization pitfalls)
    //
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Partial operations (fallback-parameter
    // style, no generic Optional). `Normalize` above carries a non-zero
    // precondition; these give callers a total path so the IsZeroLength guard is
    // written once here rather than at every call site.

    // The unit vector in the same direction as self, or fallback when self has
    // (near) zero length and no direction is defined. Total: never divides by zero.
    NormalizeOr(self: IVector, fallback: IVector): IVector
        => self.MagnitudeSquared > 0.0 ? self.Normalize : fallback;
